title: Mobile automation: what differs from the web

videos.script: This lesson is a hinge. Until now the course tested an API. From here it tests an app running on a phone. {{hinge}} The two halves share boxoffice and little else. The tools are different, the machine is different, and the things that go wrong are different. {{different}} A web page lives at an address. An app is installed, paused, killed, rotated and interrupted by a phone call. {{lifecycle}} It asks for permissions. It runs on hundreds of phone models and a dozen Android versions. And its network comes and goes. {{fragments}} So first you build the lab for this half. Android Studio, an emulator, and the command-line tools that come with them. {{lab}} Then you build Tickets, a small app that lists boxoffice's shows. Every lesson after this one tests it. {{app}} Last, how a test finds a button on a screen it cannot see. That question decides how every mobile test in this course is written. {{locate}}
